tools.description: Use this first when the user names a person, group, or chat, or asks about a conversation or relationship with someone, in their Telegram history: it turns the name into the chat `id` that the other tools take as `session`. Lists every direct and group chat, most recently active first. Returns each chat's stable `id`, which other tools accept as `session`. Only if the list exceeds the result size cap is it trimmed, with `truncated: true` and `next_offset`.

offset.description: Only to continue a truncated result: pass its next_offset.

query.description: Optional name filter (fuzzy match on names and ids)

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.title: List chats

tools.description: Use this when the user asks what is new, unread, or waiting for a reply. Lists every chat that has unread messages, with unread counts. Only if the list exceeds the result size cap is it trimmed, with `truncated: true` and `next_offset`.

offset.description: Only to continue a truncated result: pass its next_offset.

tools.name: list_unread
tools.title: List unread chats

tools.description: Use this to see what was actually said in one chat: summarize what a group has been discussing, recall a conversation with someone, or read the context around a search hit. Reads every message of one chat in an optional [since, until) time range. Returns a plain-text transcript in chronological order: a `== YYYY-MM-DD ==` line per local day, then one `HH:MM sender: text` line per message, with indented continuation lines. A senders list after the header maps each shown name to its stable account id; the account owner always appears as 我. The header also says when the chat's readable history starts: nothing earlier is available, so an empty early range means missing history, not silence. Non-text messages appear as bracketed placeholders; images show as [img:<id>], which get_media can display. There is no page size: one call returns the whole range. Only if the range exceeds the result size cap is the transcript trimmed and ends with a `[truncated]` line giving the offset to repeat the same call with. order=newest (default) keeps the latest messages when trimming, order=oldest the earliest.

contains.description: Only messages whose text contains this substring

offset.description: Only to continue a truncated result: pass its next_offset. Counted from the end of the range for order=newest and from the start for order=oldest.

sender.description: Only messages from one sender: `me` for the account owner, an account id (the ids that list_members and the message tools show), or a name exactly as those tools show it. A name several accounts share is rejected with their ids.

session.description: Chat id from list_sessions (preferred) or a display name

since.description: Inclusive start; ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

until.description: Exclusive end; ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

tools.name: read_messages
tools.title: Read a chat

tools.description: Use this when answering needs what people previously said or discussed about a topic, across private and group Telegram chats, including indirect questions that never mention Telegram or chat history (why someone decided something, who talked about a subject, what was said about a plan). Fast keyword search on the client's own index, over the full history unless `since` is given; it can miss some card and notice text, so use query_messages when completeness matters. Returns every match, newest first. Only if the matches exceed the result size cap is the result trimmed, with `truncated: true` and `next_offset`; then repeat the same call with offset=next_offset.

offset.description: Only to continue a truncated result: pass its next_offset.

since.description: ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

tools.name: search_messages
tools.title: Search messages

tools.description: Use this for exhaustive or precise lookups: everything one person said (`sender`), messages with a media type, keyword combinations with exclusions, or counting messages in a period. Structured message filter across all chats or one chat: keywords to include/exclude, media type, sender, and a time range. Each message carries `sender` (the account owner is 我) and its stable `sender_id`. Slower than search_messages but exhaustive. Covers the full history unless `since` is given; with no session, give at least one filter or `since`. Returns every match. Only if the matches exceed the result size cap is the result trimmed, with `truncated: true` and `next_offset`; then repeat the same call with offset=next_offset. To read every message of one chat in a period, use read_messages instead.

offset.description: Only to continue a truncated result: pass its next_offset.

sender.description: Only messages from one sender: `me` for the account owner, an account id (the ids that list_members and the message tools show), or a name exactly as those tools show it. A name several accounts share is rejected with their ids.

session.description: Optional chat id or display name

since.description: ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

until.description: ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

tools.title: Filter messages

tools.description: Use this for questions about who is in a group or how active its members are: who speaks most, who has gone quiet, or which members are your contacts. Lists a group's current members with each one's id, message count, and last message time, or only members who are your local contacts (friends_only).

inactive_since.description: Only members with no recorded messages since this time; ISO 8601 date/time or relative (30min, 2h, 7d, today, yesterday)

tools.title: List group members

tools.description: Use this when an image in a transcript matters to the answer. Views images from one chat. Pass the 32-character ids that read_messages and the other message tools show as [img:<id>] (images) or as the name in [视频 WxH <id>] (video cover). Returns each image the local client has cached, up to 10 per call; an id that was never downloaded reports so instead. size=preview (default) returns the client's standard copy, size=original the full-resolution copy when one was downloaded. Each image costs about as much context as a page of text, so fetch only the ones the task needs.

session.description: Chat id or display name the images were sent in
